 3 tremors in 2 days: Nagpur region no longer quake-proof? 
 Trending Kolkata Murder Delhi Building Collapse UP Murder Bengaluru Accident PM Modi Bengaluru Murder Kolkata Murder Delhi Building Collapse UP Murder Bengaluru Accident PM Modi Bengaluru Murder Kolkata Murder Delhi Building Collapse UP Murder Bengaluru Accident PM Modi Bengaluru Murder 3 tremors in 2 days: Nagpur region no longer quake-proof? 
 Sarfaraz Ahmed / Nov 10, 2026, 01:06 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Nagpur: Three earthquakes — two in Nagpur district and one in Yavatmal district — were recorded over Sunday and Monday, adding to a series of tremors that has put the seismic stability of the region under scientific scrutiny. The earthquakes were of low intensity and caused no reported damage or injuries. However, an increase in frequency of tremors has raised concerns about possible changes in geological activity beneath an area traditionally considered relatively safe from earthquakes. On Sunday, a 2.6-magnitude earthquake was recorded near Paradgaon lake, close to Umred in Nagpur district at 2.17pm at a depth of 5km. The second earthquake of 3.0 magnitude was recorded near Kalamb in Yavatmal district around 3pm on Monday, followed by a 1.9-magnitude tremor near Soholi, close to Khaparkheda in Nagpur district, at 3.28pm. The latter originated at a depth of around 4km. The latest events follow tremors near Haldgaon and Dawaha in Umred tehsil on Oct 27, including a 3.0-magnitude earthquake. With two seismic events recorded in 2023 and 11 in 2024, the recurring activity is challenging Nagpur’s perception as a low-risk seismic region. Geologists point out that the concern is not the magnitude of individual tremors but their frequency, geographical spread and possible association with dormant geological faults. Repeated stress adjustments or fault reactivation beneath the region could be responsible, although this requires detailed investigation. A stronger event cannot be ruled out merely because recent tremors have been mild. Nagpur falls under Seismic Zone II, classified as low-risk under Bureau of Indian Standards norms. However, experts caution that this classification should not lead to complacency, particularly as much of the city’s infrastructure was developed assuming relatively low seismic vulnerability. Geological Survey of India (GSI) studied 21 villages across Parseoni, Kuhi, Umred and Kamptee tehsils following the 2024 tremors, and launched a micro-earthquake survey covering nearly 1,400 sq km. It recommended continuous seismic monitoring and compliance with earthquake-resistant construction norms. Experts say the findings of these investigations need closer examination to establish whether geological structures beneath Vidarbha are becoming active again.
